producer_report.summary: The kept work already had the greedy longest-first balancing, the `shard-timings` command, the unit tests, a new coverage test in ci_shards.rs and the changelog entry. Only xtask/shard-timings.txt was missing, so I created it with one line for each of the 58 units that `test-shard 0 1 --dry-run` lists. Its values are estimates, labeled as such in the file header. Targeted tests pass.

checks_run.command: cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards --test policy --bin xtask

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A shard.rs unit test calls the real selection with a fixture timings map for n=6 and asserts that the largest per-shard duration total is at most 1.25 times the mean, and that each fixture unit appears in exactly one shard.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A shard.rs unit test includes a unit absent from the fixture timings and asserts that it is assigned to exactly one shard, with every unit still covered.
Run `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards`. The existing partition tests pass, including `shards_in_ci_yml_partition_every_workspace_test_target`, using the real checked-in xtask/shard-timings.txt.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran it: 20 passed, including shards_in_ci_yml_partition_every_workspace_test_target and the new checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace`. All pass.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A shard.rs unit test shows a malformed timings line (missing field or non-numeric seconds) returns an error that names the line.
criteria_check.evidence: shard::tests::a_malformed_timings_line_is_an_error_naming_the_line passed; asserts the message contains 'line 2' for a bad second line.

criteria_check.criterion: xtask/src/shard.rs sorts timed units by descending duration and places each on the currently least-loaded shard. Untimed units use the existing sorted index-modulo split. A new xtask subcommand that rewrites xtask/shard-timings.txt from a local run is wired in xtask/src/main.rs and listed in the usage text.
criteria_check.evidence: Read shard.rs assign(), main.rs `shard-timings` dispatch, and USAGE text mentioning shard-timings.

criteria_check.criterion: xtask/shard-timings.txt exists and has a line for every current workspace test unit that `cargo run -p xtask -- test-shard 0 1 --dry-run` lists, so the real shards are balanced rather than all falling back.
criteria_check.evidence: Created the file with 58 lines, one per unit from the dry-run; the ci_shards test checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit asserts equality with the oracle and passed. Values are labeled estimates.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing timing-balanced sharding, the timings file and the update command.
criteria_check.evidence: Read the kept CHANGELOG.md diff: entry names balanced sharding, xtask/shard-timings.txt and `shard-timings` command.

open_issues: Timings in xtask/shard-timings.txt are rough estimates (labeled in the file header), not measurements; no per-unit data was available and a full local run exceeds the time limit. Run `cargo run -p xtask -- shard-timings` and commit the result.
Full fmt, clippy and workspace tests were not run by me.
learnings: The kept work already had complete code, tests, usage text and changelog; only xtask/shard-timings.txt was missing.
desires: A cheap way to get per-target timings from the CI run without a 10-minute local suite.
